title: How to Sokkie | Basic Sokkie Shuffle for Beginners

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher introduces concepts clearly through solo breakdown before demonstrating with a partner. He emphasizes weight placement and smooth footwork while keeping instructions conversational.

lesson_structure.note: Teacher introduces himself and the channel
Teacher breaks down the basic shuffle step solo
Demonstration and breakdown with a partner

cues: Keep your feet on the ground
common_mistakes: Shifting shoulders back and forth or up and down
safety: Make sure I'm not crashing into anyone

steps_taught.name: Basic Shuffle
steps_taught.description: Shuffling forward and backward with weight mostly on the toes.

what_works: Clear distinction between leader and follower roles
Demonstrating solo first before adding a partner
what_hinders: Lack of counts or musical accompaniment during the breakdown

quotes.text: Our basic step we call a shuffle.
We never want to look like we're walking.
Top of the shoulder blade, this is the best place to kind of direct your follower.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher stands facing front with hands on hips, explaining the basic shuffle step.
Teacher demonstrates foot shuffling with arms extended as if holding a partner.

extraction.distinctive_method: Explaining foot placement by emphasizing that heels can touch the ground but weight remains on the balls of the feet.
